source: FAO Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific, Swine Health Management, Volume 2: Guide to Prevent and Control Porcine Reproductive and Respiratory Syndrome (RAP Publication 2012/27, Bangkok, 2012)
text: Practical farm-level measures to keep PRRS and similar diseases out: (1) Vehicles — use separate vehicles for inside and outside the farm; clean and disinfect any vehicle before it enters; keep the loading zone outside the farm; drivers and traders should not enter animal areas; set up a disinfectant wheel bath at farm entrances. (2) Visitors and workers — limit visitors and unnecessary contact with the pigs; require visitors and workers to change into farm-specific clothing and boots that never leave the farm; place foot baths at pen entrances and change the disinfectant daily; workers should not keep pigs at home themselves or visit live animal markets and slaughterhouses. (3) Pens and feed — clean pens of manure and waste regularly; keep feed dry and insect/pest-proof; never bring in outside fresh or frozen pig meat; bury or burn dead animals rather than allowing collection trucks onto the farm. (4) Equipment and needles — clean and disinfect tools between pens; use new or disinfected needles between batches of pigs; never borrow equipment from another farm. (5) Newly purchased animals — quarantine separately from the existing herd for at least 30 days before mixing them in.
caveat: This is a general biosecurity checklist; farmers can adapt it to their scale (scavenging, small-scale confined, or larger), but should also follow any specific instructions from local veterinary or extension staff.
